reader.requirement: At --std 85, an IF statement written with END-IF must not have the NEXT SENTENCE phrase in either position (IF c NEXT SENTENCE ... END-IF, IF c statement-1 ELSE NEXT SENTENCE END-IF): the compiler must refuse it at compile time. The witness (pb396-if-empty-consequent) does not exercise this rule at all.

edition-consulted.switches: Constructs.NextSentenceArchaic2023: a COBOL0903 archaic warning at 2023, nothing at 85; it never refuses and never looks at END-IF

reader.edition-search: Grepped src for NextSentenceStatementContext / nextSentenceStatement() (StatementBinder.BindStatement, EcBinder.ExceptionPerform, VersionConformancePass) and END_IF() (only the generated parser): no binder or validator asks whether an IF carrying NEXT SENTENCE also carries END-IF. ifStatement's END_IF? admits it by design (the PB396 determination comment on the rule, and IsNextSentenceArm's doc: 'IF Format 2's arms under an END-IF are admitted here').
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: accepted at 85 silently and at 2023 with only the archaic NEXT SENTENCE warning
reader.witnesses-cover: part: no witness exercises SR3; the cited witness is about an empty consequent

probes.printed: exit 0, stdout NEXT-1 / NEXT-2, no diagnostic
probes.expected: refused at compile time: 'If the END-IF phrase is specified, the NEXT SENTENCE phrase must not be specified' (both the THEN NEXT SENTENCE and the ELSE NEXT SENTENCE forms)

probes.printed: --std 2023: exit 0, NEXT-1 / NEXT-2, two COBOL0903 warnings (NEXT SENTENCE archaic) only
probes.expected: (2023 comparison) no 2023 format prints NEXT SENTENCE with END-IF
the legal 85 forms IF c NEXT SENTENCE. and IF c NEXT SENTENCE ELSE NEXT SENTENCE. (no END-IF) compile and run

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.16.3 SR3  (6.16.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3
OK  §1985:VI.6.16.4 GR2b  (6.16.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2b

reader.notes: The 1985 general format prints END-IF as an alternative after statement-1 or NEXT SENTENCE and SR3 is the only thing that forbids the combination; the compiler has no check for it, so IF c NEXT SENTENCE END-IF compiles and transfers to the next sentence. PB396 recorded acceptance as a 2023 cross-format latitude determination; at 85 there is no latitude because the edition's own syntax rule forbids it.
reader.at-2023: accepted, exit 0, prints NEXT-1 / NEXT-2 with two COBOL0903 archaic-NEXT-SENTENCE warnings; acceptance at 2023 is the recorded PB396 determination (no 2023 format prints the combination)
reader.repro:
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           IF WS-A = 1 NEXT SENTENCE END-IF
           DISPLAY "AFTER-IF-1".
           DISPLAY "NEXT-1".
           STOP RUN.   (WS-A PIC 9 VALUE 1; --std 85 --source-format fixed)
reader.expected: a compile-time refusal: §1985:VI.6.16.3 SR3 'If the END-IF phrase is specified, the NEXT SENTENCE phrase must not be specified.'
reader.observed: compiles with no diagnostic, runs, prints NEXT-1 (control went to the next sentence)
reader.known_note: kb/Work/PB396 (its DETERMINATION paragraph accepts IF X = 1 NEXT SENTENCE END-IF as a 2023 cross-format latitude, owner-overturnable; it does not address §1985:VI.6.16.3 SR3). No note found for the 1985 rule (grepped kb/Work for '6.16.3', 'NEXT SENTENCE END-IF').
